rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker should strive for contentment through migration, retreat, and solitude; sound solitude is better than company of contemporaries.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يجتهد في تحصيل الرضى بالهجرة والخلوة والعزلة

rows.speaker: الصائب
rows.claim: A Persian couplet praises rightly chosen solitude as better than keeping company with people of the age.
rows.anchor:
قال الصائب :
در مشرب من خلوت اكر خلوت كوراست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever leaves a beloved for God's approval receives a better beloved from God and becomes attached to it rather than the former familiar object.
rows.anchor: ومنها : أن من فارق محبوبه ابتغاء لمرضاة الله تعالى فإن الله تعالى يجعل له بدلا خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is mentioned before Ishmael so his account remains connected to Jacob's mention.
rows.anchor: قدم ذكره على إسماعيل لئلا ينفصل عن ذكر يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God purified Moses from impurities, defects, and attachment to everything besides Him; this is the passive sense of mukhlaṣ and matches ṣiddiq.
rows.anchor: أخلصه الله من الادناس والنقائص ومما سواه وهو معنى الفتح الموافق للصديق

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Sincerity in worship is a station of saints: every saint is sincere but not every sincere worshipper a saint; every messenger is a prophet but not every prophet a messenger.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : اعلم أن الإخلاص في العبودية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The active mukhliṣ purifies himself of animal and lower-soul traits; the passive mukhlaṣ is divinely adorned with spiritual, lordly qualities after purification.
rows.anchor: المخلص بكسر اللام من أخلص نفسه في العبودية بالتزكية عن الأوصاف النفسانية

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that forty mornings of sincerity cause springs of wisdom to appear from the heart on the tongue.
rows.anchor: كما قال النبي عليه السلام : "من أخلصأربعين صباحا ظهرت ينابيع الحكمة

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: A sacred report calls sincerity a secret between God and the servant and says God adorns sincere hearts through manifestations of beauty and majesty.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى : "الإخلاص سر بيني وبين عبدي لا يسعه فيه ملك مقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is accepted only from sincere servants; its degrees are exclusive worship, surrendering one's existence, and being freed from it through annihilation and subsistence in God.
rows.anchor: وفي الحقيقة لا تكون العبودية مقبولة إلا من المخلصين لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sent to creation to announce God's message; messenger is the more specific and higher designation, yet it precedes prophet here.
rows.anchor: أرسله الله إلى الخلق فأنبأهم عنه ولذلك قدم رسولا مع كونه أخص وأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tur is between Egypt and Midian; the right side means Moses' right, since the mountain has no right or left, or its auspicious side.
rows.anchor: الطور جبل بين مصر ومدين والأيمن في الأصل خلاف الأيسر أي : جانب اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call was manifested to Moses from that direction.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ندائه منه أنه تمثل له الكلام من تلك الجهة

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: The Jalalayn says Moses was traveling from Midian toward Egypt when called from a tree on the mountain's right side.
rows.anchor: قال في "الجلالين" : أقبل من مدين يريد مصر فنودي من الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Drawing Moses near was an honor, like a king bringing someone close for private conversation and chosen companionship; God spoke without an intermediary angel.
rows.anchor: تقريب تشريف مثل حاله بحال من قربه الملك لمناجاته واصطفاه لمصاحبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najiyyan is circumstantial wording attached to one of the pronouns in the call; munajat means confidential speech.
rows.anchor: ونجيا أي : مناجيا حال من أحد الضميرين في ناديناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron is the object of God's granting, an appositive to brother, and a prophet given as Moses' supporting minister in answer to Moses' prayer.
rows.anchor: مفعول وهبنا وهارون عطف بيان لأخاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift is literal as with Isaac and Jacob, but since Aaron was older, it means prophetic assistance and support.
rows.anchor: فالهبة على ظاهرها كما في قوله : {ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب}

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Moses had both spiritual effort and divine attraction: danger remains during the seeker's journey, but attraction brings gathering and safety.
rows.anchor: صاحب كشف الأسرار كويد حضرت موسى عليه السلام را هم روش بود وهم كشش

rows.speaker: جامي
rows.claim: Jami's couplet says seekers cannot arrive without the beloved's attraction, even after years of striving.
rows.anchor:
قال المولى الجامي :
339
سالكان بى كشش دوست بجايى نرسند

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Prophethood and messengership are gifts of God's mercy, not acquired by effort; even the ability to strive is God's gift.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : قوله : {ووهبنا له من رحمتنآ أخاه هارون نبيا} يشير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail is separated from his father and brother in the account to highlight special care for him; Muhammad is told to recite his ancestor's story.
rows.anchor: فصل ذكره عن ذكر أبيه وأخيه لإبراز كمال الاعتناء بأمره بإيراده مستقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail was truthful in promises made both to God and to people; a promise reports benefit before it occurs.
rows.anchor: فيما بينه وبين الله وكذا بين الناس

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Ismail's promise to God was to fulfill the obligations of worship.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : فيما وعد الله بأداء العبودية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ismail promised a companion to wait at a place and waited there for a year.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن إسماعيل عليه السلام وعد صاحبا له أن ينتظره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail also promised patience through sacrifice and fulfilled it, urging truthfulness and keeping one's word.
rows.anchor: وناهيك أنه وعد الصبر على الذبح فوفى حيث قال

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A person who promises intending to fulfill but then fails to appear is not sinful, according to a prophetic report.
rows.anchor: إذا وعد الرجل أخاه ومن نيته أن يفي فلم يف ولم يجىء للميعاد فلا إثم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise attaches to fulfilling a promise, not a threat, since causing harm is not praiseworthy; some scholars therefore allow God to waive a threat but not a promise.
rows.anchor: إن الثناء إنما يتحقق بصدق الوعد وإتيان الواعد بالموعود لا بصدق الوعيد

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh says God's promise is a right owed to obedient servants, while a threat is God's right and may be waived; pardon better fits divine generosity.
rows.anchor: وأحسن يحيى بن معاذ في هذا المعنى حيث قال الوعد والوعيد حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail was sent to Jurhum, the Amalekites, and Yemen tribes during Abraham's lifetime.
rows.anchor: إلى جرهم وإلى العماليق وإلى قبائل اليمن في زمن أبيه إبراهيم

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon identifies Jurhum as a Yemeni tribe into which Ismail married.
rows.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : جرهم كقنفذ حي من اليمن تزوج فيهم إسماعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail was a prophet who reported from God and followed Abraham's law; by scholarly consensus he had no revealed book, like Lot, Isaac, and Jacob.
rows.anchor: وكان على شريعة أبيه إبراهيم ولم يكن له كتاب أنزل إليه بإجماع العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl may mean close family through marriage or children, or the wider community reached by preaching; the first is preferable because moral improvement should begin with oneself and nearest kin.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يرجح الأول لأن الأهم أن يقبل الرجل بالتكميل على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the noblest bodily worship and zakat the best financial worship.
rows.anchor: التي هي أشرف العبادات البدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous should counsel relatives and outsiders in religious benefit.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن من حق الصالح أن ينصح للأقارب والأجانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismail pleased his Lord in speech, actions, and states; the Jalalayn explains this as fulfilling obedience.
rows.anchor: في الأقوال والأفعال والأحوال

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: The Jalalayn says Ismail was pleasing because he had fulfilled God's obedience.
rows.anchor: وفي "الجلالين" : مرضيا لأنه قد قام بطاعته

rows.speaker: بعض الصالحين
rows.claim: A righteous visitor gave six counsels: much sleep weakens tenderness of heart, much food hinders night worship, and an oppressor's company harms religious uprightness.
rows.anchor: أولها : من كثر نومه فلا يطمع في رقة قلبه

rows.speaker: بعض الصالحين
rows.claim: The counsel warns that habitual lying and backbiting threaten a faithful end, excessive social mixing removes worship's sweetness, and seeking people's approval prevents God's approval.
rows.anchor: ومن كان الكذب والغيبة عادته فلا يطمع في أن يخرج من الدنيا مع الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absolute divine approval belongs to the perfected human who gathers all perfections and realities; others are approved only in some respects or states.
rows.anchor: المرضي المطلق هو الإنسان الكامل الجامع لجميع الكمالات المحيط بحقائق جميع الأشياء

rows.speaker: روضة الخطيب
rows.claim: The cited genealogy makes Idris Noah's great-grandfather and says he was born while Adam still lived, one hundred years before Adam's death.
rows.anchor: ولد وآدم حي قبل أن يموت بمائة سنة كذا في "روضة الخطيب".

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi reports a conflicting chronology, saying Idris was born one hundred years after Adam's death.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (در جامع الأصول آورده كه ادريس بصد سال بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris was first to use scales and measures, weapons and jihad, writing, arithmetic and astronomy, sewing clothes, and wearing cotton instead of hides; he captured Cain's descendants.
rows.anchor: هو أول من وضع الميزان والمكيال وأول من اتخذ السلاح وجاهد في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though derivation from study would not normally explain the name's declension, Idris may have been named for extensive study in his language; he reportedly received thirty scrolls.
rows.anchor: فلقب به لكثرة دراسته إذ روى أنه تعالى أنزل عليه ثلاثين صحيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siddiq means constant truthfulness in every state; nabi distinguishes Idris, since not every truthful person is a prophet.
rows.anchor: ملازما للصدق في جميع أحواله

rows.speaker: عباس بن عطاء
rows.claim: Abbas ibn Ata ranks the lowest station of messengers above the highest of prophets, and each lower spiritual rank above the one beneath it.
rows.anchor: قال عباس بن عطاء : أدنى منازل المرسلين أعلى مراتب النبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris was raised to the fourth heaven; the Mi'raj account places Adam in the first, John and Jesus in the second, Joseph in the third, Aaron in the fifth, Moses in the sixth, and Abraham in the seventh.
rows.anchor: وهو السماء الرابعة فإن النبي عليه السلام رأى آدم ليلة المعراج في السماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree whether Idris is alive or dead in heaven; the majority say he is alive, and the author calls that correct.
rows.anchor: فالجمهور على أنه حي وهو الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source counts Khidr and Ilyas alive on earth and Idris and Jesus alive in heaven.
rows.anchor: أربعة من الأنبياء في الأحياء اثنان في الأرض وهما الخضر والياس

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi relates that Idris prayed for the angel bearing the sun, afflicted by its heat; God accepted, and the angel visited and carried Idris toward sunrise, where Idris learned of his appointed death.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در رفع ادريس اخبار متنوعه هست ابن عباس فرمودكه روزى ادريس

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Another report says the Angel of Death longed to meet Idris, took his soul at his request by God's command, restored it, then carried him through Hell to Paradise, from which he never emerged.
rows.anchor: وروايتي ديكر آنست كه ملك الموت از كثرت طاعت ادريس مشتاق ديدارش شد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised place is the sun's sphere: seven spheres lie below and seven above, and it is their axis and source of illumination, like the heart in the body.
rows.anchor: فالآية دلت على رفعته وعلى علو مكانه وهو فلك الشمس أما رفعته فبتبعية مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those refers to the prophets from Zechariah through Idris, whom God favored with religious and worldly gifts, outward and inward.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى المذكورين في هذه السورة من زكريا إلى إدريس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lineage clauses trace prophets through Adam, Noah's passengers, Abraham, and Israel; Ibrahim descends from Sam, while Moses, Aaron, Zechariah, John, and Jesus descend from Jacob.
rows.anchor: وهم من عدا إدريس فإن إبراهيم كان من ذرية سام بن نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Jesus descends through Mary, the verse shows that daughters' children count among their mother's forebears' descendants.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن أولاد البنات من الذرية لأن عيسى من مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about those guided and chosen is explanatory if attached to the prophets, partitive if attached to Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: قالوا من فيه للتبيين إن عطف على من النبيين وللتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets heard revealed promises and warnings, then prostrated and wept; believers should imitate them despite their high lineage and rank.
rows.anchor: أي : آيات الترغيب والترهيب في كتبهم المنزلة

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A prophetic report urges reciting the Quran with tears or making oneself weep if unable.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "اتلوا القرآن وابكوا فإن لم تبكوا فتباكوا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the eyes do not weep, hearts should grieve at hearing the Quran, which descended in sorrow upon the sorrowful.
rows.anchor: إن لم تبك أعينكم فلتبك قلوبكم يعني تحزنوا عند سماع القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaf with an open lām means good descendants and with a still lām evil descendants; those following the prophets were bad successors.
rows.anchor: يقال لعقب الخير خلف بفتح اللام ولعقب الشر خلف بالسكون

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: The Jalalayn identifies the later evil people as Jews, Christians, and Magians.
rows.anchor: وفي "الجلالين" بقي من بعد هؤلاء قوم سوء يعني اليهود والنصارى والمجوس

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A prophetic report says each prophet had followers who kept his practice, then successors appeared who said what they did not do and did what was forbidden; resisting them by hand, tongue, or heart is faith.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "ما من نبي بعثه الله في أمة إلا كان له من أمته حواريون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Squandering prayer may mean abandoning it, delaying it past its time, ruining its reward through slander and lies, or praying without intention and humility.
rows.anchor: تركوها أو أخروها عن وقتها أو ضيعوا ثوابها بعد الأداء بالنميمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following desires includes wine and permitting a paternal half-sister; Ali describes conspicuous buildings, showy mounts, and celebrated clothing.
rows.anchor: من شرب الخمر واستحلال نكاح الأخت من الأب

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ali describes the people as building conspicuous structures, riding showy mounts, and wearing famous clothing.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه هم من بنى المشيد وركب المنظور

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report to David compares the world to a carcass around which dogs compete and says fine food, soft clothes, and fame cannot coexist with Paradise.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "أوحى الله إلى داود مثل الدنيا كمثل جيفة اجتمعت عليها الكلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ease in satisfying desires is no sign of salvation; Umar refused cold water with honey because he feared answering for it.
rows.anchor: ومن ثمة امتنع عمر رضي الله عنه من شرب ماء بارد بعسل

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb reports two angels meeting in the fourth heaven: one was ordered to bring a desired fish to a Jew, the other to spill oil desired by a worshipper.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه : التقى ملكان في السماء الرابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desire literally means wishing; here it means blameworthy objects. Hawa is the blameworthy subset, while desire can be praiseworthy if it leads to good.
rows.anchor: والشهوة في الأصل التمني ومعناها بالفارسية (آرزو خواستن) والمراد بها في الآية المشتهيات المذمومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayy means evil in Arab usage; every evil is ghayy and every good is rashad.
rows.anchor: فإن كل شر عند العرب غي فكل خير رشاد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets ghayy as the requital of wrongdoing, comparing it to atham as punishment for sin.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك جزاء غي كقوله تعالى {يلق أثاما}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view calls Ghayy a valley in Hell whose heat other valleys seek refuge from, prepared for grave sinners including adulterers, wine drinkers, usurers, and those who abandon prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل غي واد من جهنم يستعيذ من حره أوديتها

rows.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
rows.claim: Saadi's couplet warns against obeying the lower self because its desires and qibla continually change.
rows.anchor: مبر طاعت نفس شهوت يرست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repentant turn from shirk and sins, choose faith instead of disbelief, and perform good after remorse; God admits them to Paradise.
rows.anchor: رجع من الشرك والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those admitted to Paradise lose none of their reward and are denied nothing; injustice can mean reduction or withholding.
rows.anchor: فالظلم بمعنى النقص والمنع وشيئا مفعوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eden may be part of the many gardens, a proper name for one garden, or a name for the whole abode of reward; its sense of permanent dwelling fits the context.
rows.anchor: وجنات عدن علم لجنة مخصوصة كشهر رمضان وقد يحذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The special gardens of Eden and Firdaws are stations of the near ones rather than places common people enter by default.
rows.anchor: فإن جنة عدن المخصوصة وجنة الفردوس لا يدخلهما العوام بالأصالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise is made while the garden is unseen or the servants cannot see it; calling God Rahman signals the mercy behind promise and fulfillment.
rows.anchor: أي : وهي غائبة عنهم غير حاضرة أو غائبين عنها لا يرونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive servants implies sincere worship rather than worship of world, self, or desire, and thus special honor of Eden.
rows.anchor: وفي الإضافة إشارة إلى أن المراد من يعبده مخلصا له في العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised destination is certain: ma'tiy can mean the promised person will come to it or that it is surely coming.
rows.anchor: فالمأتي بمعنى المفعول من الإتيان أو بمعنى الفاعل أي : جائيا ألبتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghw means idle talk without benefit; its absence in Paradise indirectly teaches people to avoid it in this life.
rows.anchor: فضول كلام لا طائل تحته وهو كناية عن عدم صدور اللغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected: inhabitants hear angels or one another greeting with peace instead of idle speech.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أي : لكن يسمعون تسليم الملائكة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning and evening provision means it continues without interruption; alternatively, food is served at those times although Paradise has only perpetual light.
rows.anchor: والمراد دوام الرزق كما يقال أنا عند فلان صباحا ومساء يراد الدوام

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says divine descriptions appeal to each people's favorites: ornaments, silk, and couches for different cultures, breakfast and supper for Arabs.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام في تفسيره فإن قيل المقصود من الآيات وصف الجنة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading identifies the provision as seeing God, with a report that the most honored look upon His face morning and evening.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : {ولهم رزقهم فيها} من رؤية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That refers to the garden already described; the phrasing magnifies it and identifies its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الجنة المذكورة المتقدمة يريد تلك التي بلغك وصفها

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: One parsing makes the demonstrative and garden a subject and predicate; another makes garden an apposition with the following clause as predicate.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : مبتدأ وخبر جيء به لتعظيم شأن الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives the garden as inheritance without human choice; its heirs avoid shirk and sins, obey, and are preserved in it.
rows.anchor: نورثها ونعطيها بغير إختيار الوارث

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: Inheritance is a simile: deeds lead to Paradise as lineage leads to inherited property, but the garden is ultimately God's gift and mercy, against the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: قال في "الأسئلة المقحمة" : كيف قال نورث والميراث ما انتقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance is especially strong ownership because it cannot be rescinded, reclaimed, voided, or forfeited.
rows.anchor: والوراثة أقوى ما يستعمل في التملك والاستحقاق من حيث أنها لا تعقب بفسخ

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says the pious inherit Paradise homes that would have belonged to people of Hell had they believed and obeyed.
rows.anchor: وقيل يورث المتقون من الجنة المساكن التي كانت لأهل النار لو آمنوا

rows.speaker: المولى الفناري
rows.claim: Al-Fanari divides gardens into divine allotment for those unable to act, inherited homes for believers, and gardens earned through differing deeds; every act has its reward, as with Bilal's two post-ablution prayers.
rows.anchor: قال المولى الفناري في تفسير الفاتحة : اعلم أن الجنات ثلاث

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that Gabriel delayed his visit and cited neglected nail and moustache trimming, cleaning finger joints, and tooth-stick practice before reciting this verse.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : أبطأ الملك على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم أتاه فقال له

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A prophetic report commands cleaning finger joints where grime collects; al-Qurtubi says hardened dirt can retain impurity and block water from the skin.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "نقوا براجمكم" وهي مفاصل الأصابع والعقد التي على ظهرها

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes connect the verse with questions about the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; revelation was delayed fifteen or forty days while the Prophet awaited an answer.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين : هو حكاية لقول جبريل حين استبطأه رسول الله

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Gabriel says he is a commanded servant: when sent he descends, and when held back he waits; the verse and Surat al-Duha then came down.
rows.anchor: فقال جبريل : إني كنت أشوق ولكني عبد مأمور إذا بعثت نزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanazzul is gradual descent; angels descend only at God's command and when His wisdom requires it.
rows.anchor: والتنزل النزول على مهل لأنه مطاوع للتنزيل والمعنى قال الله لجبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What lies ahead means future afterlife affairs, what is behind means past worldly affairs, and what lies between means the present until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي : بالاختصاص {ما بين أيدينا} من الأمور الأخروية الآتية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading interprets the phrases as eternal decree, everlasting governance, and everything between pre-eternity and eternity.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {له ما بين أيدينا} من التقدير الأزلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording resembles God's statement that He knows what is before and behind them.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : {يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not forgetful: He does not abandon Muhammad when revelation is delayed for wisdom, or is not inattentive.
rows.anchor: فعيل بمعنى فاعل من النسيان بمعنى الترك أي : تاركا لك كما زعمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted He is predicates the phrase: God owns the heavens, earth, and their creatures, so forgetfulness cannot be ascribed to Him.
rows.anchor: من الخلق فكيف يجوز النسيان على الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship means carrying out what one is commanded and undertaking obedience to commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: والعبادة قيام العبد بما تعبد به وتكلف من امتثال الأوامر والنواهي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inward worship involves body following the Law, self opposing its desires, heart turning from world to afterlife, secret detaching from both realms for God, and spirit surrendering existence for witnessing.
rows.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" : {فاعبده} بجسدك ونفسك وقلبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persist through worship's hardships; do not grieve over delayed revelation, mockery, or enemies' delight, because God watches over and cares for you.
rows.anchor: اصبر لمشاقها ولا تحزن بإبطاء الوحي واستهزاء الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām implies standing firm for worship through trials, unlike the ʿalā in the command about family prayer.
rows.anchor: وتعدية الاصطبار باللام لا بحرف الاستعلاء كما في قوله {واصطبر عليها}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samiy means namesake, partner, equal, or likeness; the verse denies anyone worthy of God's name or any being called God alongside Him.
rows.anchor: السمي الشريك في الاسم والمثل والشبيه أي : مثلا يستحق أن يسمى إلها

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says even idolaters never called their objects Allah; divine majesty protected this supreme name while believers invoke it in ease and hardship.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يكى از آثار سطوت آلهي آن بودكه هي كس ازاهل شرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet calls the divine name a wondrous charm of the heart and a complete remembrance of the soul.
rows.anchor: الله الله ه طرفه نامست اين حرزدل وردجان تمامست اين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anecdote says a ruler who called himself Allah died when his insides burned; Pharaoh called himself the highest lord but could not claim to be Allah.
rows.anchor: روي أن بعض الجبابرة سمى نفسه بلفظ الجلالة فصهر ما في بطنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says no one may be named al-Rahman except God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا يسمى أحد الرحمن وغيره

rows.speaker: المولى الفناري
rows.claim: Al-Fanari says Allah is exclusive in designation and use, Rahman in use, and Rahim is not exclusive; calling Musaylima Rahman was deliberate unbelief.
rows.anchor: قال المولى الفناري في ترتيب أسماء البسملة : إن لاسم الجلالة اختصاصا وضعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh accused a Yamama teacher called Rahman of teaching Muhammad; the answer identifies God as his Lord and teacher, and divine names such as Rahman or Creator should not be assigned to people.
rows.anchor: قالت قريش لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلغنا أنك إنما يعلمك رجل باليمامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet changed the name al-Aziz because a servant's proper condition is humility and submission.
rows.anchor: العزةوشعار العبد الذلة والاستكانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker is Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who crushed a decayed bone and mocked the claim that people would be raised alive after death.
rows.anchor: أبي بن خلف حين فت عظما باليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase is placed first to stress disbelief that life follows death; the lām intensifies the denial and works with future sawfa.
rows.anchor: تقديم الظرف وإيلاؤه حرف الإنكار لما أن المنكر كون ما بعد الموت وقت الحياة

rows.speaker: التكملة
rows.claim: An alternative says the lām quotes the Prophet's claim that the dead will be raised alive, rather than emphasizing the disbeliever's statement.
rows.anchor: وفي "التكملة" اللام في قوله تعالى : {لسوف} ليست للتأكيد

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Al-Bahr says the emphatic lām requires an implicit subject and predicate, originally we will surely emerge alive; the preceding mā also intensifies the denial.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" لما كانت هذه اللام لام الابتداء المؤكدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question rebukes the claim; remembrance here means reflection after knowledge has lapsed.
rows.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار التوبيخي والواو لعطف الجملة المنفية على مقدر

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Radi says the nūn resembles wāw through its nasal resonance, explaining its deletion in yakun.
rows.anchor: وقال الرضي : النون مشابه للواو في الغنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first created humans from nothing, so the One who began without material can restore scattered matter; this concise proof establishes resurrection by analogy with first creation.
rows.anchor: بل كان عدما صرفا فيعلم أن من قدر على الابتداء من غير مادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By an oath, God will gather deniers alive from their graves and gather the devils who misled them, each disbeliever chained to his devil.
rows.anchor: لنجمعه القائلين بالسوق إلى المحشر بعد ما أخرجناهم من الأرض أحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will be brought around Hell on their knees because the severe event leaves them unable to stand.
rows.anchor: جمع جاث من جثا يجثو ويجثي جثوا وجثيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets jithiyyan as gathered groups, a reading also chosen by the Jalalayn.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما جثيا جماعات جمع جثوة

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi glosses nanzia' as bringing out; shia means a following, people, or faction.
rows.anchor: لنخرجن قاله البغوي والنزع الجذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God extracts the most rebellious person from each faction; ayyum can be a relative clause with omitted wording or a quoted interrogative.
rows.anchor: والمقصود أنه يميز من كل طائفة منهم الأعصى فالأعصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misleaders deserve more punishment than passive followers, as the cited verse says; the author applies this threat especially to Ubayy.
rows.anchor: إذ عذاب الضال المضل يجب أن يكون فوق عذاب من يضل تبعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence is resurrection, gathering, presentation near Hell, selecting the worst rebels, then entering the Fire.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن أول الأمر البعث ثم الحشر ثم الإحضار ثم النزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who most deserves the Fire; ṣilyan means entering it.
rows.anchor: وهم المنتزعون يقال صلى يصلي كلقي يلقي ومضى يمضي إذا دخل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every person reaches and enters Hell; its being a decree means this is inevitable.
rows.anchor: أي : واصل جهنم وداخلها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says everyone descends into the hell of natural desire and cannot escape by nature alone; God saves those He rescues.
rows.anchor: ففيه إشارة إلى أن كل وارد يرد بقدم الطبيعة في هاوية الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unjust are wrongdoers through disbelief and sins; God leaves them kneeling in Hell, humbled and unable to move toward Paradise.
rows.anchor: لأنفسهم بالكفر والمعاصي {فيها} في جهنم {جثيا}

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: The Jalalayn interprets the kneeling ones as the whole assembly.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير "الجلالين" جثيا أي : جميعا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilite threat theologians argue that whoever enters Hell never leaves.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن الوعيدية وهم المعتزلة قالوا : إن من دخلها لا يخرج منها

rows.speaker: المرجئة
rows.claim: The Murji'a say believers do not enter Hell and read warud as mere presence rather than entry.
rows.anchor: وقالت المرجئة لا يدخلها مؤمن قط وقالوا أن الورود ههنا هو الحضور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl al-Sunna allow sinful believers to be punished and then released; they read warud as entry, supported by verses about Pharaoh's people, Hell's fuel, and the promised rescue.
rows.anchor: فأما أهل السنة فقالوا يجوز أن يعاقب الله العصاة من المؤمنين بالنار ثم يخرجهم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crossing the bridge counts as entering for purposes of warud, even though the saved are distant from Hell and do not hear it.
rows.anchor: الصراط فالمرور في حكم الورود وفي الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahillat al-qasam is the amount done to fulfill an oath, an idiom for a very small amount.
rows.anchor: والتحلة مصدر حللت اليمين أي : أبررتها وتحلة القسم

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A prophetic report says a Muslim whose three children die avoids the Fire except for the brief fulfillment of the oath identified with this verse.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "لا يموت لمسلم ثلاث من الولد فيلج النار إلا تحلة القسم"

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says believers pass by Hell through fever touching the body; reports call fever each believer's share of the Fire and an expiation.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد ورود المؤمن النار هو مس الحمى جسده في الدنيا

rows.speaker: جابر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Jabir reports that personified fever was sent to Quba; when the people complained, the Prophet offered relief or purification, and they chose purification.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر رضي الله عنه استأذنت الحمى على رسول الله عليه السلام فقال

rows.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet told her not to curse fever because it is commanded and taught a prayer asking it to depart; she said it and the fever left.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها قدمنا المدينة وهي أوبى أرض الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quranic signs are clear in miraculous proof and meaning; the disbelievers are Nadr ibn al-Harith and companions addressing poor believers.
rows.anchor: واضحات الاعجاز والمعاني وهي حال مؤكدة فإن آيات الله لا ينفك عنها الوضوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may mark speech addressed to believers or spoken about them; maqam means residence and nadi a council gathering leaders and supporters.
rows.anchor: أي : لفقراء المؤمنين واللام للتبليغ كما في مثل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers groomed and perfumed themselves, boasted of worldly prosperity over poor believers, and argued true faith would bring better worldly conditions to divert them from religion.
rows.anchor: قالوا مفتخرين بالحظوظ الدنيوية على فقراء المؤمنين لو كنتم على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarn is explained by min qarn; each age's people are a generation for those after them, and Kashifi defines a qarn as a group gathered in one time.
rows.anchor: كم فعول أهلكنا ومن قرن بيان لإبهامها وأهل كل عصر قرن لمن بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athath means household furniture; r'ya means outward appearance and derives from seeing.
rows.anchor: تمييز عن النسبة وهو متاع البيت يعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples including ʿAd and Thamud had more worldly goods and appearance than Quraysh yet were destroyed, showing bounty did not mark divine favor and warning Quraysh.
rows.anchor: كثيرا من القرون التي كانوا أفضل منهم فيما يفتخرون به من الحظوظ الدنيوية كعاد وثمود

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi's couplet says neither wealth nor beauty saved earlier peoples from destruction and punishment.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (نه آن مال هلاك از ايشان دفع كرد ونه آن جمال عذاب

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading contrasts seekers who discipline and humble themselves with deniers who indulge in wealth, pride, and desire; earlier nations were destroyed by love of the world and status.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن أهل الإنكار وأهل العزة بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command addresses those boasting of wealth; whoever remains sunk in error is extended either to remove excuses or through gradual entrapment.
rows.anchor: مغمورا بالجهل والغفلة عن عواقب الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those persisting in error receive this extension, since some misguided people are guided; Rahman is named because respite belongs to temporal mercy.
rows.anchor: لما أن المد لا يكون إلا للمصرين عليها إذ رب ضال يهديه الله

rows.speaker: شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: The author's master glosses extension as entrapment through longer life, wider wealth, and more children, or respite with continued favors until punishment arrives.
rows.anchor: قال شيخي وسندي قدس سره في بعض تحريراته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking someone gradually through comfort is more painful than swift punishment; extension begins from the Merciful, not names of severity.
rows.anchor: لأن الأخذ على طريق التدريج والنعمة أشد منه على طريق التعجيل والنقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extension lasts until they see the promised outcome; plural verbs follow the conditional's meaning while earlier singular pronouns follow its form.
rows.anchor: غاية للمد الممتد وجمع الضمير في الفعلين باعتبار معنى من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outcome is worldly defeat and captivity by Muslims or punishment at Resurrection; these alternatives do not exclude each other because afterlife punishment is certain.
rows.anchor: فإنه إما العذاب الدنيوي بغلبة المسلمين واستيلائهم عليهم وتعذيبهم إياهم

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi argues that even a prosperous misbeliever with a long life ends in punishment here or hereafter, so worldly gifts will not help him.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أي : لو فرض أن هذا الضال المتنعم قد مد له في أجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they witness their fate, they learn which party truly has the worse place, contrary to their boast.
rows.anchor: بأن يشاهدوا الأمر على عكس ما كانوا يقدرونه فيعلمون أنهم شر مكانا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi contrasts believers' levels of Paradise with disbelievers' levels of Hell.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (س بدانند آنرا كه بدترست از هر دو كروه

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Al-Bahr explains that describing the place as evil establishes evil for its inhabitant.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : جعلت الشرارة للمكان ليفيد إثباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will be weaker in faction and supporters, not possess the fine council claimed; defeat exposes their lack of an independent rescuing party.
rows.anchor: فئة وأنصارا لا أحسن نديا كما كانوا يدعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the astray, the verse independently explains that God increases believers in faith, deeds, certainty, and guidance.
rows.anchor: كلام مستأنف سبق لبيان حال المهتدين أثر بيان حال الضالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lasting good deeds are an independent divine statement about the guided, not part of disbelievers' quoted speech; they outlast boasts and transient goods and have the better end.
rows.anchor: كلام مستأنف وارد من جهته تعالى لبيان فضل أعمال المهتدين

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says disbelievers may have status and wealth here but face ruin later, while believers receive guidance and protection now and reward and a good return later.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي يعني (اكر كافر انرا دفردنيا جاه ومال است

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A little finite harm followed by unending benefit is better than the reverse; worldly respite is no sign of merit, nor limited worldly means a sign of inferiority.
rows.anchor: ففي الآية إشارة إلى أن الضرر القليل المتناهي الذي يعقبه نفع كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyat salihat includes all afterlife deeds and good words; a report compares remembrance phrases to leaves blown from a tree, erasing sins.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الباقيات الصالحات هي أعمال الآخرة كلها ومنها الكلمات الطيبة

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet calling remembrance phrases lasting deeds and treasures of Paradise, to take up before access is lost.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه : جلس رسول الله عليه السلام ذات يوم وأخذ عودا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading reserves lasting deeds for acts arising from divine inspirations in hidden hearts; actions rooted in the self's nature and reason do not qualify.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : الباقيات الصالحات هي الأعمال الصالحات التي هي من نتائج الواردات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person should refine and purify the self so lasting deeds and excellent states grow from it; the author likens this to fruitful seed and productive marriage.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يجتهد في إصلاح النفس وتزكيتها ليتولد منها الأعمال الباقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage was revealed about al-As ibn Wa'il, who owed Khabbab money, demanded rejection of Muhammad, then mocked resurrection by claiming wealth and children and promising repayment there.
rows.anchor: نزلت فيمن سخر بالبعث وهو العاص بن وائل كان لخباب بن الأرت عليه مال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative conveys astonishment at the man's outrageous and brazen claim; the construction means look at the disbeliever in God's signs.
rows.anchor: والهمزة للتعجب من حاله والإيذان بأنها من الغرابة والشناعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative has two hamzas; the root means climbing to a mountain's top or a mountain pass.
rows.anchor: همزته استفهام وأصله أأطلع من قولهم اطلع الجبل إذا ارتقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt asks whether he reached God's unique knowledge of the unseen or made a covenant with its Knower; only those routes could disclose future wealth and children.
rows.anchor: أقد بلغ من عظمة الشأن إلى أن ارتقى إلى علم الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the covenant as testimony of faith and righteous action, for which God promised reward.
rows.anchor: وقيل العهد كلمة الشهادة والعمل الصالح فإن وعد الله بالثواب عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rejects the claim; God records his lies, disbelief, and mockery and will lengthen the punishment he deserves instead of increasing money and children.
rows.anchor: ليس الأمر على ما يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death God inherits what he says, meaning the wealth and children received in this world; his future boast has no object beyond them.
rows.anchor: أي : مسمى ما يقول ومصداقه وهو ما أوتيه

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The cited commentary says God strips away what He gave him.
rows.anchor: كما في "الإرشاد"

rows.speaker: العيون
rows.claim: The cited source parses mā as appositional: God destroys him and transfers wealth and children to someone else.
rows.anchor: وقال في "العيون" ما بدل من هاء نرثه بدل اشتمال

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi paraphrases this as inheriting the wealth and children he claimed would be given to him tomorrow.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (وميراث ميكيريم آنه ميكويدكه فردا بمن خواهند داد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He comes alone on the Day of Resurrection, without wealth or children from this life, much less any added share.
rows.anchor: وحيدا خاليا لا يصحبه مال ولا ولد كان له في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deluded claim fortunes and offspring in this life and salvation and rank in the next, mocking renunciants; they fail to see attachment brings distance and leaves them unsupported.
rows.anchor: أهل الغرور يدعون الإحراز للفضيلتين المال والولد في الدنيا والنجاة

rows.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
rows.claim: Al-Kamal al-Khujandi's couplet says breaking the idol of conceit in the lovers' faith is better than a hundred acts of worship.
rows.anchor:
قال الكمال الخجندي :
بشكن بت غروركه دردين عاشقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh polytheists made idols gods apart from God, hoping for honor through intercession, connection to God, and rescue from punishment.
rows.anchor: أي : مشركوا قريش {من دون الله ءالهة}

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One admonition says honor cannot come from humiliation through asking people; seek God, remember Him, or accept His decree to be honored in both worlds.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : كيف تظفر بالعز وأنت تطلبه في محل الذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rejects their expectation: the gods will disown their worship when they see its evil outcome and become enemies to their worshippers.
rows.anchor: سينكر الكفرة حين شاهدوا سوء عاقبة كفرهم عبادتهم لهم

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: The Jalalayn says inanimate idols deny worship because they did not know they were worshipped; God will make them speak and ask Him to punish their worshippers.
rows.anchor: وقال في تفسير الجلالين {سيكفرون بعبادتهم} أي : يجحدونها

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: In the Jalalayn's reading, both pronouns refer to the idols, who become adversaries and helpers against their worshippers.
rows.anchor: فالضمير في يكفرون ويكونون للآلهة
